label: Sarah Little
narrative: Little is one of the small number of people who work across both of the serious civil research programmes, which makes her a useful index of how thin the actual technical bench is. A marine biochemist trained through the MIT/Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution joint programme, she sits on the board of the Scientific Coalition for UAP Studies, where she co-authored the 2023 study of reported UAP shape, size, kinematics, electromagnetic effects and sound with Robert Powell and Larry Hancock, and she is a co-author on the Galileo Project's 2025 paper in Geoscientific Instrumentation, Methods and Data Systems describing the deployment of a geomagnetic variometer station as auxiliary instrumentation for UAP study. That paper is a small but important artefact: it is a mainstream Copernicus-published instrumentation paper, in a geophysics journal, about hardware installed specifically to look for UAP signatures. The transferable point is that the same handful of researchers - Little, Knuth, Cloete, Szydagis, Watters - appear across SCU, UAPx and Galileo, which is why the total civil analytical capacity is far smaller than the volume of public discussion implies.
